description: A3 write-side backstop: a symlink may NEVER be created into a governed zone on ANY channel, allowlist-BLIND. The reader-side half of A3 (a symlink-following read of a planted plan/manifest) is a timing/IO property exercised in-process by tests/test_write_guard.py + tests/test_hooks.py, not by this block/allow corpus; this row covers the WRITE side that write_guard enforces. Two attempts are clean regression gates that earned-the-red on pre-fix HEAD: (a1) ``ln -s X cc`` targets the BARE governed directory ``cc`` — pre-fix ``_is_protected`` matched only paths UNDER ``cc/``, so planting a symlink AT ``cc`` itself was ALLOWED (plant primitive); (a3) an MCP ``create_symlink`` whose ``path`` is an allowlisted leaf (``cc/blueprints/x.json``) — pre-fix the allowlist permitted the write, so a symlink could be planted in an operator-writable subtree. a2 (``cp -s``) and a4 (PowerShell ``New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink``) broaden the deny across the cp and PowerShell channels. The fix: allowlist-blind symlink-creation deny across Bash ``ln``/``cp -s``/``--symbolic-link``, MCP symlink verbs (``_is_mcp_symlink_verb`` + ``_mcp_leaf_denied``), and PowerShell ``New-Item``/``ni``; ``_is_protected`` now matches the bare governed dir. This is the regression gate that keeps the A3 write-side fixed.
